translationRepairs: She bore a son, Dezheng; at four [years] she became a widow.
She bore a son, Dezheng; when he was four she became a widow.
After 生子德政, 四歲而寡 dates Dezheng's age at her widowhood, not Lady Su's; the original literal is ambiguous and readily read as her own age.
Her mother-in-law, Lady He, went to fetch water from the brook and was gone a long time.
Her mother, Lady He, went to fetch water from the brook and was gone a long time.
母何氏 is Lady Yao's mother; 姑 would be required for a mother-in-law, so the idiomatic in-law rendering is invented.
She suddenly heard a splash, rushed outside, and saw a tiger carrying her mother-in-law away in its mouth.
She suddenly heard a splash, rushed outside, and saw a tiger carrying her mother away in its mouth.
其母 continues 母何氏 from the preceding sentence and names Lady Yao's mother, not a mother-in-law.
Yao carried her mother-in-law home, nursed her with medicine, and cared for her for more than twenty years until her death.
Yao carried her mother home, nursed her with medicine, and cared for her for more than twenty years until her death.
負母 is the same mother; nothing in the unit supports 姑 or a mother-in-law.
Her husband's uncle was too ill to travel, so Zhang went back to prepare his medicine and meals and brought a sedan chair with her.
Her father-in-law was too ill to travel, so Zhang went back to prepare his medicine and meals and brought a sedan chair with her.
In this wife-biography 舅 is paired with 姑: husband and mother-in-law guarded the stockade while 舅 remained behind ill, so he is the father-in-law, not an uncle.
Her father-in-law's younger brother, because of illness, had not gone; Zhang returned to attend to medicines and food, and moreover had a sedan chair follow her of her own accord.
Her father-in-law, because of illness, had not gone; Zhang returned to attend to medicines and food, and moreover had a sedan chair follow her of her own accord.
舅 is the father-in-law left at home; 'father-in-law's younger brother' adds a kinship the Chinese does not state.
When bandits arrived, she ordered the sedan bearers to carry her uncle away while she herself faced the raiders.
When bandits arrived, she ordered the sedan bearers to carry her father-in-law away while she herself faced the raiders.
其舅 is the same 舅 already identified as the father-in-law who had not traveled, not a husband's uncle.
Before long bandits arrived; she immediately ordered that the sedan chair carry her uncle, while she herself encountered the bandits.
Before long bandits arrived; she immediately ordered that the sedan chair carry her father-in-law, while she herself encountered the bandits.
其舅 continues that father-in-law; the literal 'uncle' is the same kinship error.
One soldier slashed her left arm, yet she yielded all the more stubbornly.
One soldier slashed her left arm, yet she was all the more unyielding.
愈不屈 means she became even less yielding; 'yielded all the more' inverts the negation 不屈.
The bandits rushed in and pulled her out.
The bandits vied to pull her out of the water.
'Rushed in' is wrong after she had thrown herself into the river, but 出之 is extracting her from the water, not the bandits themselves rushing out; 競 marks them vying to pull her up.
Li Shun'er was the daughter of Li Rang, a scholar of Xuzhou.
Li Shun'er was the daughter of Li Rang, a scholar of Xu Prefecture.
許州 is Xu Prefecture; the following unit's 密邇許昌 confirms Xuchang, not 徐州 (Xuzhou).
Li Shun'er was the daughter of Li Rang, a Confucian scholar of Xuzhou.
Li Shun'er was the daughter of Li Rang, a Confucian scholar of Xu Prefecture.
The same 許州 is Xu Prefecture near Xuchang, not Xuzhou.
In Zhizheng 16 Zhang Shicheng besieged Hangzhou. His daughter Lin'annu cried out in alarm, "The rebels are here—Mother, forgive me, but I must find a way to die."
In Zhizheng 16 Zhang Shicheng besieged Hangzhou. Huang Zhongqi's daughter Lin'annu cried out in alarm, "The rebels are here—Mother, forgive me, but I must find a way to die."
其女臨安奴 belongs to the Huang Zhongqi–Lady Zhu household just introduced; 別母 and later 朱氏母子 show she is not Zhang Shicheng's daughter.
In the sixteenth year of Zhizheng, Zhang Shicheng attacked Hangzhou; his daughter Lin'annu said in alarm, "The bandits are here—I take leave of my mother to seek death."
In the sixteenth year of Zhizheng, Zhang Shicheng attacked Hangzhou; Huang Zhongqi's daughter Lin'annu said in alarm, "The bandits are here—I take leave of my mother to seek death."
其女 is Huang Zhongqi's daughter, not Zhang Shicheng's; the proposed parenthetical 'his (Huang Zhongqi's)' is accurate in sense but awkward English.
Yulian hanged herself too. Three women had taken their own lives, and the bandits killed them all.
Yulian then hanged herself as many as three times, and the bandits killed her as well.
玉蓮因自縊者凡三 records three hanging attempts by Yulian, and 賊並殺之 is the bandits then killing her as well; the original invents three women, whom the Chinese does not name.
Her father Defu taught in the lake and Xiang region. Tongzu was one of his students, and Defu gave him his daughter in marriage.
Her father Defu taught in the Hu and Xiang region. Tongzu was one of his students, and Defu gave him his daughter in marriage.
湖、湘間 is the Hu and Xiang region as a paired toponym, not a generic lake plus the Xiang River.
For his military service Qi was promoted to assistant magistrate of Qianshan Subprefecture, and Lady Luo was granted the title Proper Person.
For his military service Qi was promoted to assistant magistrate of Qianshan Subprefecture, and Lady Luo was granted the title of Yiren.
宜人 is the honorary rank title Yiren; 'Proper Person' is an opaque calque, not the title as used.
Qi was promoted to Assistant Magistrate of Qianshan Subprefecture for military merit; Lady Luo was enfeoffed as Yiren.
Qi was promoted to Assistant Magistrate of Qianshan Subprefecture for military merit; Lady Luo was granted the title Yiren.
封宜人 confers an honorary wifely title, not a territorial enfeoffment.
Wishing to defile her, she then with her son Rong'er and daughter Huiniang threw herself from a cliff and died.
Wishing to defile her, she together with her son Rong'er and daughter Huiniang threw themselves from a cliff and died.
投崖而死 covers mother and both children, but the proposed 'she ... threw themselves' is ungrammatical; the verb must be plural with an explicit together-with phrase.
Ne served as Censor; he died early, and Liu preserved her resolve without wavering.
Ne served as Investigating Censor; he died early, and Liu preserved her resolve without wavering.
監察御史 is the office of investigating censor, not the generic word Censor.
His daughter-in-law Lady Liu, stiffly pressing upon her mother-in-law's corpse, cursed incessantly; the soldiers killed them both.
His daughter-in-law Lady Liu, stiffly pressing upon her mother-in-law's corpse, cursed incessantly; the soldiers killed her as well.
The mother-in-law was already killed in the previous sentence (見殺); 兵並殺之 records that the soldiers then killed Lady Liu as well, not that they killed both at once.

Taizhou suffered military attack; Zongyuan was then in mourning for her mother-in-law, enduring death to guard the coffin; she was seized by roving soldiers and threatened with coercion. Yuan said, "If I feared death, how could I have stayed here!

Taizhou suffered military attack; Zongyuan was then in mourning for her mother-in-law, risking death to guard the coffin; she was seized by roving soldiers and threatened with coercion. Yuan said, "If I feared death, how could I have stayed here!
忍死護柩 means she braved or held out against death to guard the coffin; 'enduring death' is unintelligible English while she is still alive.

The couple were captured by the army. When they reached Yutian County, a man who coveted Lady Song's beauty and wished to kill Zongren—Lady Song said to her husband, "Fate has brought me to this pass. I will not let my body become your ruin."

The couple were captured by the army. When they reached Yutian County, there was a man who coveted Lady Song's beauty and wished to kill Zongren. Lady Song said to her husband, "Fate has brought me to this pass. I will not let my body become your ruin."
The original breaks off after the relative clause and never completes the sentence before Lady Song speaks; the repair restores a grammatical English sentence without changing the Chinese sense.
Xu Youtou's wife, Lady Yue, was from the capital.
Xu Naotou's wife, Lady Yue, was from the capital.
猱 is náo; Youtou does not transcribe 猱頭.
Xu Youtou's wife Lady Yue was a native of the capital.
Xu Naotou's wife Lady Yue was a native of the capital.
The literal field repeats the same unmatched transcription of 猱頭; Naotou is the correct pinyin.

When the capital fell, she said to her daughter, "Your father has gone out to defend the city. I hold the rank of a third-grade consort, and you are both a scholar's daughter and a jinshi's wife. We cannot endure disgrace."

When the capital fell, she said to her daughter, "Your father has gone out to defend the city. I am a titled lady of the third rank, and you are both a Confucian family's daughter and a jinshi's wife. We cannot endure disgrace."
三品命婦 is a titled official's wife of the third rank, not an imperial consort; 儒家女 is a daughter of a Confucian family.
